title: OpenAI scientist proposes shared limits on frontier AI development
summary:
OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has proposed that frontier AI developers agree on shared capability limits based on perplexity and other measures, and refrain from crossing them until their ability to monitor and understand model behavior meets defined safety milestones. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman endorsed the proposal, but Pachocki specified no initial threshold, start date or enforcement mechanism. It remains a call for an industry agreement, not an adopted restriction [reuters.com#1][openai.com#1][biggo.com#1][shattered.io#1].

Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token, with lower scores indicating better predictions. Pachocki says the metric can track pretraining progress as task-based tests become outdated. He argues that AI could accelerate research into pretraining methods as early as 2027, potentially outpacing improvements in safety monitoring [openai.com#1][reuters.com#1].

He also acknowledged that perplexity alone cannot provide a common yardstick: labs use different training mixtures and evaluation data, and the measure misses some capability gains from reasoning after pretraining. Pachocki’s proposal calls for shared evaluation, red-team and transparency standards alongside staged limits, with further development dependent on concrete advances in monitoring [lavx.hu#1][unite.ai#1][mlq.ai#1].
quote: I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone
talking_points: Published scores: OpenAI reported log-perplexity of about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 and 0.91 for GPT-4; Pachocki linked scores below 0.8 to emerging mathematics and cybersecurity capabilities, and cited results on open math problems at about 0.76 [openai.com#1][lavx.hu#1][mlq.ai#1].

What drove the curve: OpenAI attributed most of the steep decline in its 2026 loss curve to long-term research and compute investment, with AI automation contributing a smaller share [mlq.ai#1][unite.ai#1].

Uncertain next threshold: Pachocki forecast further transformative capabilities as log-perplexity reaches 0.68–0.70, but said their nature is unknown and current evaluations may not test for them [lavx.hu#1][mlq.ai#1].

Policy debate: The Straits Times reported that Democrats’ midterm gains could renew congressional scrutiny and efforts to introduce AI safety rules, while President Donald Trump opposes broad restrictions on AI development [straitstimes.com#1].

perspectives.text: Jakub Pachocki, OpenAI chief scientist: Pachocki said publishing OpenAI’s internal measurements gives competitors a clearer view of the company’s position, but he judged shared safety measures more urgent than that competitive cost [openai.com#1][lavx.hu#1].
Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft AI chief executive: Suleyman publicly called Pachocki’s proposal “super important” and praised OpenAI for making the case for transparency [dealroom.co#1].

Alexandr Wang, Meta AI executive: Wang warned that technological progress could outpace people’s ability to understand or control its consequences and called for urgent advances in safety, alignment and security [tradingview.com#1].

title: AI sell-off exposes risks in data-center financing
summary:
The AI-stock sell-off has intensified scrutiny of the debt and corporate guarantees financing data-center expansion. Nvidia’s guarantees totaled $118 billion as of Oct. 25, while its commitments to smaller cloud providers were estimated at $32 billion over the next several years. On a Nov. 17 earnings call, interim chief executive Colette Kress said Nvidia would scrutinize AI cloud companies’ financial strength and prioritize sites with visible, durable demand [thebanker.com#1].

Those commitments have helped reassure lenders financing data centers and computing clusters. But analysts warn that banks may now be less willing to extend bridge loans to smaller providers whose debt they expect to resell. Nvidia’s tighter scrutiny could affect companies that lack established revenue or strong backers [thebanker.com#1][businessinsider.com#2].

Jon von Tetzchner, CEO and co-founder of San Francisco-based Vivaldi, questioned whether many AI applications are useful. An unnamed worker at a major San Francisco AI company told the BBC he expected a downturn and feared it would affect him [yahoo.com#1][bbc.com#1].
quote: On GPU-backed loans to unrated borrowers, credit committees will become much more selective because no bank wants to get stuck holding unsellable bridge loans on its own balance sheet.
quote_author: Henning Stein, finance fellow at Cambridge Judge Business School
talking_points: Policy watch: Investors were awaiting U.S. October personal consumption expenditures inflation data, scheduled for Wednesday during a shortened holiday week [indiatimes.com#1].

IPO signal: Anthropic’s record $107 billion initial public offering raised much more than expected but failed to lift shares of backers Google and Amazon or offering partners Broadcom, AMD and Nvidia [sfexaminer.com#1].

City spillover: San Francisco’s AI boom has brought business to services such as Paw Perk, a dog-walking service for startup offices. Rents and house prices have risen, while office vacancies have fallen [bbc.com#1].

Additional financing: Nvidia, Google and Microsoft participated in a concurrent $26 billion private placement, bringing combined gross proceeds from the IPO and placement to more than $107 billion [cryptobriefing.com#1].

AI labels: Vivaldi co-founder Jon von Tetzchner likened companies’ rush to adopt AI labels to the earlier blockchain and crypto boom. He said some use popular technology labels to attract investors despite a questionable connection to their existing businesses [yahoo.com#1].

Long contracts: The disclosed commitments include multiyear purchases and equipment leases extending as far as 2045; $186.2 billion in fixed commitments include termination rights or conditions [247wallst.com#1].

Market losses: Taiwan’s Taiex lost more than $500 billion in market value over the week, while South Korea’s Kospi shed more than $1.8 trillion from its June peak, according to Financial Times estimates [ft.com#1].
AI spending: Gartner projected global AI-related investment of $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027 [aljazeera.com#1].
Investor flows: Goldman Sachs data showed hedge funds had sold global equities for a third consecutive week, with short sales exceeding long purchases by 1.5 to 1 [bloomberg.com#9].

Regional demand: Santa Lucia Asset Management CEO Florian Weidinger warned that China’s shift toward domestic AI hardware could restrict Nvidia’s access to Asia, while competition from more chipmakers and weaker demand could squeeze margins and prompt order revisions [cnbc.com#4].
Enterprise demand: Anthropic had 11,900 customers, with more than 100 generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue, according to figures reported around the listing [cryptobriefing.com#1].
China’s buying measures: Chinese exchanges also announced transaction-fee cuts, and Shenzhen proposed a market-making mechanism for its ChiNext board [cnbc.com#1].
Investor rationale: Notable Capital said its research found developers chose Claude over ChatGPT 70% of the time, reversing the prior year’s pattern [techcrunch.com#1].

GIC: The Singapore sovereign wealth fund said Claude Code’s popularity among developers and model improvements driving enterprise adoption informed its investments in Anthropic [techcrunch.com#1].
South Korean finance ministry and financial regulators: Officials said long-term AI growth expectations remain intact and warned against excessive anxiety or panic selling [ft.com#1].

Dillin Wu, Pepperstone strategist: Wu said the support measures may steady prices temporarily but are unlikely to reverse the reassessment of AI-related valuations or draw foreign investors back [yna.co.kr#1].

JPMorgan analysts: The bank’s analysts described the pullback as mostly AI-related deleveraging and said they still viewed the AI growth cycle as durable, citing lower leverage and improved positioning [indiatimes.com#1].

title: Anthropic mathematician says Claude outpaced him near proof's finish
summary:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says the company’s Claude AI took a larger role as they worked on a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a famous problem about prime numbers. Alpöge said he guided the effort by combining two mathematical ideas, but Claude moved faster than he did near the end. Separate Lean and Mathlib groups have since verified the formalized proof [ifanr.com#1][theguardian.com#2].

The collaboration lasted about six weeks, from early October to Nov. 16, according to Alpöge’s account [cryptobriefing.com#1]. He has not yet published a readable mathematical explanation, leaving researchers to work out the argument behind the computer-checked result [scmp.com#1][cryptoslate.com#1].

The announcement came a day after Anthropic’s stock-market debut, prompting questions about its timing. Alpöge called the timing “horrible” and said he would have finished earlier if he could. He denied that the release was coordinated with the listing [theguardian.com#2][scmp.com#1].
quote: It’s a monumental moment in human history. It’s really the biggest thing I think that’s ever happened in mathematics
talking_points: A specific advance: While extending Stepanov’s method, Claude proposed setting the theta-lift chain length to √X, which Alpöge said helped move the work forward [ifanr.com#1].
Scope: Alpöge said the proof also covers the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions [cryptoslate.com#1].
Company process: Alpöge said he consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before publishing [taipeitimes.com#1].

perspectives.text: Nestor Guillen, New York University mathematics professor: Guillen said Alpöge’s work was a more human-directed collaboration than OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes announcement, with AI working “more like a tool” rather than appearing as an autonomous authority [taipeitimes.com#1].

Shing-Tung Yau, Fields Medal-winning mathematician: Yau said machines still lag people in posing problems even as their problem-solving ability grows, and suggested mathematical research could increasingly find results first and examine them afterward [scmp.com#1].

title: Study finds coding-agent instruction files grow 226% over time
summary:
A new study of AI coding-agent instructions found that files such as CLAUDE.md grew by 226% over their lifetimes as additions outpaced deletions across 1,867 repositories. Researcher Kushal Chakrabarti analyzed 247,694 instruction lifetimes and attributed the pattern to agents’ imperfect recall of why older instructions were added [arxiv.org#1].

The paper, revised Nov. 20, reports that comments recording the reasoning behind instructions cut excess prompt size by 99.3% in constructed tests. In small-scale tests in real repositories, the approach also improved instruction-following by 17.7% [arxiv.org#1]. The coding agent Claude Code is also being used for projects beyond conventional software development, including hobbyist-built apps and hardware prototypes [tomsguide.com#1][xda-developers.com#1]. A separate review of the free coding agent Freebuff warns that it logs mouse and keyboard input and may use submitted information for advertising and AI training [notebookcheck.net#1].
quote: If English is the new code, why don't we have comments yet?
talking_points: Prompt drift: The paper measured a net increase of 4.7 instructions per commit and found that the chance of deleting an instruction falls geometrically as it ages [arxiv.org#1].

Tuning workflow: Sybil Solutions’ open-source skill benchmarks local-model serving using interleaved control runs, a memory cap and long-context checks. ExplainX says it did not independently rerun the published performance figures [explainx.ai#1].

Prototype hardware: One Claude Code project used an ESP32-C3, motion sensor and OLED display in an hourglass prototype that controls iPhone app access. Its planned 211-LED circuit board still needs to be manufactured and tested [xda-developers.com#1].
Paid access: Claude Code is not included in Anthropic’s free subscription, and Tom’s Guide lists Claude Pro at $20 a month as the starting paid plan [tomsguide.com#1].

title: Microsoft warns AI-driven patching could fuel months of further outages
summary:
Microsoft President Brad Smith warned Sunday that technology outages could continue for months as companies and governments race to patch vulnerabilities and upgrade aging systems. His warning follows separate failures affecting U.S. aviation, Microsoft services, banks, Apple and the National Security Agency; intelligence officials say they have found no evidence the incidents were coordinated cyberattacks [theverge.com#1][newsweek.com#1][indianexpress.com#1][theguardian.com#1].

Smith said artificial intelligence is making it easier for defenders to find software flaws, but those discoveries can also help attackers, while rushed fixes leave less time for testing. Older infrastructure adds to the risk: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said some critical systems, including internet-connected firmware and industrial equipment, cannot readily be patched [newsweek.com#1][techradar.com#1].

Smith said Microsoft’s own outage was not caused by AI or a cyberattack, but by an interaction between an earlier software update and a newer one that changed network traffic. The company has published two incident reports, completed nine corrective measures and identified 13 more, he said [nationalheraldindia.com#1][newsweek.com#1].
quote: The whole information infrastructure of the world is in effect being upgraded right now.
talking_points: IT strain: A cybersecurity professional told the Guardian that the relentless exposure of software flaws had left their team “exhausted” [theguardian.com#1].
Exploit pressure: The FBI warned Nov. 13 that hackers were using the open-source AI tool ARTEX, with some intrusions reaching administrator access in under three hours [geekwire.com#1].
Flight impact: The Federal Aviation Administration’s ground stop led to more than 18,000 canceled flights [theguardian.com#1].
Patch volume: Microsoft fixed 1,413 vulnerabilities in October, exceeding its previous full-year record, according to Oren Etzioni’s analysis [geekwire.com#1].

System design: IGEL Chief Technology Officer John Walsh said critical infrastructure should be built to keep essential services running when a component is compromised or unavailable [newsweek.com#1].

perspectives.text: Microsoft: Brad Smith called for closer cooperation between technology companies and governments to share information about emerging cyber threats [nationalheraldindia.com#1].
Oren Etzioni: Etzioni expects Windows, iOS and Chrome to become more secure than ever within a year or two as AI helps find and fix a finite supply of bugs [geekwire.com#1].

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent: Bessent said Americans should not worry about the stability of financial institutions, describing banks as among the most resilient U.S. companies after decades of cybersecurity investment [newsweek.com#1].

title: Apple plans spring 2027 launches for five iPhone, iPad and Mac products
summary:
Apple is reportedly preparing five product updates for February or March 2027: the iPhone 18 and lower-cost iPhone 18e, an entry-level iPad, a new MacBook Neo and a MacBook Air with an M6 chip. A second group—the iPhone Air 2, OLED iPad Air and refreshed iPad Pro—is expected later in the first half of the year, possibly in late March or April. Apple has not announced the products, specifications or launch dates [macrumors.com#1][9to5mac.com#1][gadgets360.com#1][dantri.com.vn#1].

The first-wave iPhones are expected to use Apple’s A20 chip and 9GB of memory, while the entry-level iPad could gain Apple Intelligence support. Reports say the MacBook Neo may move from an A18 Pro chip and 8GB of memory to an A19 Pro and 12GB; the later iPad Air is expected to add an OLED screen, and the iPad Pro may use a vapor-chamber cooling system [macrumors.com#1][macobserver.com#1][computerbild.de#1].

The staggered schedule follows Apple’s decision to release its premium iPhones in autumn while holding back the standard iPhone 18 for spring. The reported calendar places the first releases in the iOS 27.4 cycle, but the company has not confirmed the schedule [36kr.com#1][ifanr.com#1][firstpost.com#1].

Siri updates: A report says iOS 27.3, expected in December 2026, will add support for Siri’s multi-step actions in Apple apps, with full support for third-party apps deferred until 2027 [ifanr.com#1][huxiu.com#1].
Price pressure: The MacBook Neo’s U.S. starting price reportedly rose from $599 at launch to $699 in June 2026, while the next model’s price remains unknown [maclife.de#1].

The new game puts players in the roles of Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a criminal couple in the fictional, Florida-inspired state of Leonida. Lucia is the franchise’s first non-optional female lead, and their relationship is central to the story alongside the series’ open-world crime and satire [npr.org#1][laist.com#1]. The game launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles; Rockstar has not announced a date for its online mode [benchmark.pl#1][tuoitre.vn#1].

title: Signal blocks mobile AI agents from capturing private chats
summary:
Signal has added protections to block operating-system AI assistants from reading chats on iOS 27 and Android, saying screen access could expose conversations outside its encrypted messaging service [bleepingcomputer.com#1][indianexpress.com#1][samaa.tv#1]. On iOS, the app blocks screenshots and recordings by default, hides chats from the App Switcher and prevents Siri AI from viewing its screen. On Android, it enables Screen Security when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen [macobserver.com#1][dailynewsegypt.com#1].

Signal says messages can be captured after the app decrypts them for display and then made available to an AI system’s local database or remote server, beyond Signal’s control [dailynewsegypt.com#1][dobreprogramy.pl#1]. Users can turn off the protection, but Signal warns that doing so could expose their own messages and those of their contacts. The app cannot offer the same protection on macOS; Signal advises Mac users to exclude it from Siri in system settings [macobserver.com#1][bleepingcomputer.com#1]. Signal is asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for clearer technical documentation and a way for developers to opt apps out of AI access [forklog.com#1][dobreprogramy.pl#1].
quote: We will now be taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where we can detect an AI assistant attempting to read your Signal screen
talking_points: Earlier protection: Signal introduced a safeguard in May 2025 to block Microsoft’s Recall screen-capture feature from capturing chats in its Windows 11 app [bleepingcomputer.com#1][t3n.de#1][securityaffairs.com#1].
Temporary override: On iOS, users can temporarily disable screenshot blocking; Signal restores it automatically after 10 minutes [macobserver.com#1].

Other access routes: Signal says screenshot controls cannot prevent agents from reading app data through device files, while third-party agents such as Meta Muse may use Android Accessibility permissions [betanews.com#1][forklog.com#1].

Messages at risk: Signal’s concern extends to disappearing messages: a separate screen-capture system such as Microsoft Recall could use optical character recognition to read them and store searchable records [dobreprogramy.pl#1][benchmark.pl#1].

title: Delta restores Atlanta flight system after outage delays 1,000 flights
summary:
Delta Air Lines restored its automated aircraft weight-and-balance system on Sunday after an outage delayed about 1,000 flights, or 67% of its schedule, as Thanksgiving travel approached. Flight operations were still recovering after automation returned. Delta attributed roughly 70% of delays and cancellations tracked by FlightAware to the outage and the rest to weather [wfla.com#1][prensalibre.com#1].

The system calculates aircraft weight and balance before departure. Crews use that information to confirm a plane can fly safely. Delta used manual procedures while working to restore the system, and the Federal Aviation Administration said its air-traffic systems were not involved. The agency issued a roughly hour-long ground stop for some flights into Atlanta, Delta’s largest hub. Delta had about 5,000 flights scheduled Sunday, according to the airline [theverge.com#1][wfla.com#1][prensalibre.com#1].

Holiday demand: Hartsfield-Jackson officials expected more than 4 million passengers to pass through Atlanta between Nov. 19 and Dec. 1, 5% above the same period last year [nation.com.pk#1].
Manual loading: Without automation, Delta staff had to count baggage and prepare loading reports before departures [firstpost.com#1][businessinsider.com#1].
Passenger assistance: Delta said it was rebooking customers and providing meals and hotel rooms when needed, with refunds available for canceled flights [wfla.com#1].
Holiday demand: AAA projected 81.5 million Americans would travel at least 50 miles from home during the Thanksgiving period, Nov. 24-30 [finchannel.com#1].

title: UN climate summit ends without pact as fossil fuel dispute stalls talks
summary:
The COP31 United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Nov. 22 without an overarching agreement after nearly 200 countries failed to resolve disputes over fossil fuels and climate finance. The talks ran about two days past their scheduled close, making COP31 the longest COP conference on record. The final draft omitted an explicit reference to fossil fuels, prompting the European Union, the United Kingdom, Panama and vulnerable island states to reject it [bbc.co.uk#1][theguardian.com#1][pbs.org#2].

The draft referred indirectly to the 2023 COP28 commitment to transition away from fossil fuels but did not spell out a pathway or reaffirm the wording. Oil-producing countries, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, resisted explicit references to fossil fuels, while poorer countries objected that the proposal did not set concrete funding levels for adaptation. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen said fossil fuels and finance were the main obstacles; summit president Murat Kurum said he would not put forward a replacement draft [mercopress.com#1][scmp.com#2][dawn.com#1].

Countries agreed on separate measures, including a program to support workers and communities through the energy transition and a plan to assess adaptation progress. More than 80 countries backed Türkiye’s proposed goal of raising electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, but the goal was not part of an adopted overarching pact. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he would seek advice on possible reforms to the consensus-based negotiating process. The next summit is scheduled for Addis Ababa [insideclimatenews.org#1][mercopress.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1][tass.com#1].
quote: Temperatures keep shattering records. Climate extremes keep intensifying. Emissions remain far too high. And every delay makes our task harder and more costly.
talking_points: Emissions record: A 440 Megatonnes analysis found Canada had cut emissions 8.5% from 2005 levels by 2023, compared with an average 32% reduction across the other G7 countries [theglobeandmail.com#1][lethbridgeherald.com#1].

Electricity target: The proposed 35% electricity share by 2035 compares with about 23% today. Coal supplies roughly one-third of global electricity and fossil gas about one-fifth, so the emissions effect would depend on how the power is generated [investing.com#1][rfi.fr#1].

Australian fallout: Australian opposition leader Angus Taylor called for Climate Minister Chris Bowen to resign, while Prime Minister Anthony Albanese did not say whether he would dismiss him [straitstimes.com#2].

Finance gap: The draft dropped a proposed annual adaptation-finance figure of $120 billion, while estimated adaptation needs in the Global South alone totaled about $500 billion a year [theconversation.com#1][tass.com#1].

Emissions gap: The UN Environment Programme’s modeled pathway requires greenhouse-gas emissions to fall 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 from 2025 levels. Full implementation of current national pledges would cut emissions far less, putting the world on an estimated 2.6°C warming trajectory [finchannel.com#1].

Legal challenge: Climate advocates have asked the Federal Court to require Ottawa to bring its 2030 emissions plan into compliance with the Net-Zero Accountability Act, which sets no fines or penalties for missed targets [theglobeandmail.com#1][ledevoir.com#1].

Carbon removal: The draft's explicit reference to carbon dioxide removal would have been a first in a COP final agreement. Natural approaches such as tree planting face limits of scale and permanence, while technological options remain controversial and not well advanced [bbc.co.uk#2].

Science dispute: The final days also saw disagreement over the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s work, with UK climate negotiator Kate Hughes saying the draft moved backward on science [thelocal.dk#1].

US absence: The United States sent no delegation for the second consecutive year after President Donald Trump’s administration withdrew from the Paris climate agreement [cbsnews.com#1][straitstimes.com#1].

COP initiatives: At the Turkey talks, Canada announced up to $10 million for climate-risk and early-warning systems; nearly 100 countries separately backed a proposal to raise electricity’s share of final energy use to 35% by 2035 [theglobeandmail.com#2].

perspectives.text: European Union: Speaking for the bloc, Irish Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said it would not endorse a climate decision that failed to mention fossil fuels, arguing that the omission did not reflect the science or the action required [pbs.org#1].

Saudi Arabia and Russia: Saudi Arabia’s delegate Mohammad Ayoub said Arab countries had negotiated in good faith and accounted for only a small share of historical emissions, while Russia warned that moving away from fossil fuels too quickly could cause fuel poverty [mercopress.com#1].

Like-Minded Developing Countries: India’s representative Amandeep Garg said the draft inadequately reflected equity, historical responsibility and developed countries’ climate-finance obligations, especially in its proposed global targets [firstpost.com#2].

Türkiye COP31 presidency: President Murat Kurum said the presidency had not imposed the text and accepted that countries lacked consensus; Türkiye’s presidency also denied giving any country preferential treatment during the talks [pbs.org#1][al-monitor.com#3].

Climate-process reform advocates: Nikki Reisch of the Center for International Environmental Law argued that requiring every country to agree on every detail is not fit for a climate emergency; former Vice President Al Gore called for a process reflecting majority positions [dawn.com#2].

Canada’s environment minister: Julie Dabrusin’s office emphasized clean-energy projects, electrification and cooperation with provinces, territories and Indigenous Peoples [theglobeandmail.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#2].

Greenpeace Canada: Senior energy strategist Keith Stewart argued the government is avoiding a direct admission that it has abandoned the 2030 target and said Prime Minister Mark Carney is driving those policy choices [theglobeandmail.com#1][lethbridgeherald.com#1].

Former environment minister Catherine McKenna: She argued that an agreement omitting fossil fuels would be worse than no deal and said Canada risks being left with stranded assets if other countries move more quickly into clean energy [theglobeandmail.com#2].

Lavanya Rajamani, University of Oxford professor of international environmental law: Rajamani said the impasse showed a widening gap between climate science and political action, as governments’ appetite for costly measures diminishes while the world approaches a 1.5°C overshoot [time.com#1].
European Union: The bloc said it could not support a text that failed to address the implementation gap [downtoearth.org.in#1].

Global Climate and Health Alliance: Executive Director Jeni Miller said the outcome failed to provide a clear fossil-fuel transition plan or financing for countries to prepare their health systems for climate shocks [globalissues.org#1].

This is a modeled pathway, not a prediction that those outcomes will occur [finchannel.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: Did the collapse cancel commitments made at earlier climate summits?
suggested_qna.answer: No. The failure to adopt an overarching agreement did not erase existing commitments under prior COP decisions or the Paris Agreement [abc.net.au#2][energylivenews.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: Where will countries resume climate negotiations?
suggested_qna.answer: Countries are expected to discuss unresolved issues at interim meetings in Bonn before COP32, scheduled for Addis Ababa [tass.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: Did the failed summit cancel climate commitments countries had already made?
suggested_qna.answer: No. The failure to adopt a new political declaration did not erase obligations or technical and legal frameworks agreed at previous UN climate conferences [abc.net.au#1].

historical_background: The 2015 Paris Agreement established a goal of limiting warming to 1.5°C above preindustrial levels [npr.org#1][theconversation.com#2]. title: Suspected Ukrainian drones sink Russian corvette, hit second ship off Libya
summary:
Libya’s eastern administration said a suspected drone attack caused an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at Benghazi on Sunday. Satellite imagery identified the vessel as the Russian navy corvette Merkury and showed it capsized, with only its bow above water [al-monitor.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1][dw.com#1]. Two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press that Ukrainian sea drones launched from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya struck the ship. They said four drones were intercepted and two hit. Ukraine has not claimed responsibility, and Russia has not commented [abcnews.com#1][cbsnews.com#1].

Medical sources said 10 people, including Russians and Libyans, suffered minor injuries. Later Sunday, a drone boat hit a second vessel off Benghazi, reportedly a Malta-flagged commercial ship. Libyan naval forces rescued its crew. Military sources said Libyan forces intercepted more than 20 drone boats off the coast [al-monitor.com#1][rferl.org#1].

The eastern administration said it would investigate jointly with Russia. Its prime minister, Osama Hamad, said the government had formally asked the U.N. General Assembly and Security Council for an international inquiry, including into suspicions that the drones came from western Libya. The U.N. mission in Libya called for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation [al-monitor.com#1][euronews.com#2].
quote: Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts
quote_author: United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL)
talking_points: U.N. request: Hamad also asked the U.N. to verify whether Ukrainian experts are in Libya and called on Kyiv to explain their activities [al-monitor.com#1].
Russian operations: Russia has used Benghazi as a logistical hub for its military operations in Africa and its Mediterranean presence, according to The Hill [thehill.com#1].
Distance from front: Benghazi is more than 1,000 miles from southern Ukraine [theguardian.com#1][firstpost.com#1].
Diplomat’s statement: Ukraine’s top diplomat in Washington wrote that the vessels would “no longer be serving the Russian war machine,” without explicitly claiming responsibility [rferl.org#1].

perspectives.text: Eastern Libyan administration: It described the suspected strike as a violation of Libyan sovereignty and maritime safety and said it reserved the right to take legal and diplomatic action against anyone found responsible [al-monitor.com#1].

Government of National Unity in Tripoli: It warned that foreign forces using Libyan facilities outside official state channels could draw external conflicts into the country and called for the military to be unified under state authority [trtworld.com#1].

Jalel Harchaoui, Libya specialist at the Royal United Services Institute: He said Ukraine was likely responsible, while stressing that his view was an informed judgment rather than an official attribution [bbc.co.uk#1].

timeline.content: Uprising toppled Muammar Gaddafi, leaving rival administrations in Libya [bbc.co.uk#1].
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine [al-monitor.com#1].
Ukraine said it struck a Russian-linked oil tanker in the Mediterranean [theglobeandmail.com#1].
Russia accused Ukraine of attacking an LNG carrier off Libya [euronews.com#2].
Ukrainian drones struck Merkury’s sister corvette Boikiy near St Petersburg [defence-blog.com#1].
A drone hit Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Baltic Sea [thehill.com#1].
Explosion and suspected drone attacks hit vessels near Benghazi [al-monitor.com#1][rferl.org#1].

title: Democrats secure 258 House seats, setting up divided government
summary:
Democrats have secured at least 258 of 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives, their largest majority since 1992, after North Carolina Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Virginia Foxx in a recount. Republicans hold at least 173 seats, with four contests unresolved. Democrats also won a 56-seat Senate majority, giving them control of both chambers under Republican President Donald Trump beginning in January [abcnews.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1][thehindu.com#1].

Democrats say their first 100 days will focus on the cost of living and health care, including votes to reverse Republican Medicaid cuts and restore expired Affordable Care Act tax credits. They also plan investigations into the administration and the finances of Trump and his family. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, expected to become speaker, has not ruled out another impeachment effort [scmp.com#1][ft.com#1].

Trump can veto legislation passed by the Democratic majorities. The four outstanding House races include contests in Minnesota and Tennessee and two Louisiana runoffs scheduled for December; the results could increase the Democrats’ majority [bbc.co.uk#1][euronews.com#1].
quote: If you don’t feel a sense of urgency and pressure in this job, and a desperation to deliver for folks, then you don’t belong under this Capitol dome.
talking_points: Narrow recount: Hubbard beat Foxx by 330 votes; North Carolina law allows a recount when the margin is below 1% [bbc.co.uk#1][gandul.ro#1].
Caucus differences: Rep. Troy Carter says Democrats are “not a monolith” and members bring different ideas [scmp.com#1].
Competitive districts: A Democratic campaign committee memo said the party won 70 of the 92 House districts it had identified as battlegrounds [folha.com.br#1].
Senate leadership: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer [aa.com.tr#1].

perspectives.text: White House: The administration warned that proposed Democratic investigations could amount to “blatant criminality” [abcnews.com#1][ft.com#1].

Sen. Mark Kelly: The Arizona Democrat says Congress should investigate the Iran war’s strategy and spending, asking who set the targets and why tens of billions of dollars in munitions were used [ft.com#1].
President Donald Trump: After saying he would accept the election results and work with Democrats, Trump posted an image of a red cap marked “VETO” [thehindu.com#2][elpais.com#1].
Rep. Jim Jordan: The Ohio Republican, selected to lead House Republicans in the minority, said the party would fight to regain power [euronews.com#1][business-standard.com#1].

timeline.content: Voters cast ballots in midterm elections for Congress [thehindu.com#2][aa.com.tr#1].
Trump issued an order seeking to limit information Congress can obtain [ft.com#1].
Hubbard won the recount by 330 votes, flipping Foxx’s North Carolina seat [abcnews.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].
Senate Democrats are scheduled to choose their party leader [aa.com.tr#1].

title: Israeli settler arson attacks prompt investigation and political clash
summary:
Suspected Israeli settlers torched at least a dozen Palestinian vehicles and several homes and spray-painted racist slogans in at least four villages in the occupied West Bank overnight Saturday into Sunday, residents and Israeli authorities said. No injuries were reported. Police opened an investigation, and Israeli forces deployed to Deir as-Sudan, Deir Abu Masha’al, Kafr Malik and At-Tuwani [france24.com#1][theguardian.com#1][abc.net.au#1].

Gadi Eisenkot, the opposition leader tasked with forming Israel’s next government, called the attacks “Jewish terrorism” and urged arrests and severe sanctions. He blamed policies pursued by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich. Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attacks, while Ben-Gvir accused Eisenkot of prejudging the investigation and courting Arab-party support [france24.com#1][ynetnews.com#1].

An October 27 election left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu without a parliamentary majority. President Isaac Herzog assigned Eisenkot to form a government, but coalition talks remain unresolved. Eisenkot has until December 6, with a possible 14-day extension, to secure a majority. If no one succeeds in forming a government, another election is due next year [newarab.com#1][brasildefato.com.br#1].
quote: At the moment, we don't see any real attempts by the Israeli authorities to stop it. A condemnation is not enough.
talking_points: Village damage: Residents and local reporting counted seven burned vehicles in Kafr Malik, three in Deir Abu Mashal and two in Deir as-Sudan [ynetnews.com#1].

Violence frequency: The U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs recorded an average of six settler attacks a day in the West Bank in 2026; a U.N. tally cited by CNN counted 410 attacks linked to the olive harvest since September [abc.net.au#1][krdo.com#1].
Security resources: The Israel Defense Forces said the incidents diverted military resources from other security work, including counterterrorism operations [washingtonpost.com#1][ynetnews.com#1].
Enforcement dispute: B’Tselem spokesperson Yair Dvir said condemnation alone was insufficient, arguing Israeli authorities had made no real effort to stop the attacks [abc.net.au#1].
Outpost reference: Graffiti reading “Greetings from Susya” appeared to refer to the recent evacuation of an Israeli settler outpost in the southern West Bank [abc.net.au#1][thejc.com#1].

perspectives.text: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s national security minister: Ben-Gvir rejected Eisenkot’s characterization, saying Eisenkot did not know the facts of the case or the investigation. He accused Eisenkot of offering political support to Arab lawmakers in exchange for their backing for a government [ynetnews.com#1].

Gideon Saar, Israel’s foreign minister: Saar described the assailants as a handful of extremists who did not represent law-abiding residents and said Israeli authorities were committed to enforcing the law [france24.com#1].

Yair Golan, leader of Israel’s Democrats party: Golan warned that failure to stop settler violence could lead to a third intifada and said the current government was providing cover and support for the violence [theguardian.com#1].
Yair Dvir, B’Tselem spokesperson: Dvir said public condemnation did not amount to a meaningful effort by Israeli authorities to halt settler attacks [abc.net.au#1].
Yousef Jabareen, head of Israel’s Joint List: Jabareen attributed the attacks to the occupation and government policies that, he said, had made violence against Palestinians routine [scmp.com#1].

timeline.content: Hamas-led attack on Israel preceded an escalation in West Bank violence [scmp.com#1].
Israeli election left Netanyahu without a parliamentary majority [newarab.com#1].
President Herzog assigned Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government [presstelegram.com#1].
Israel’s parliament was sworn in without a new government [newarab.com#1].
Police investigated fires and vandalism in four West Bank villages [france24.com#1][theguardian.com#1].
Eisenkot faces his initial deadline to form a government [brasildefato.com.br#1].

did_you_know: In Kafr Malik, graffiti reading “Greetings from Susya” appeared to invoke a recently evacuated settler outpost [abc.net.au#1].

More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements there alongside about three million Palestinians; the United Nations and most countries regard the settlements as illegal, while Israel disputes that position [dw.com#1][scmp.com#1]. Violence in the territory has risen since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the ensuing Gaza war; at least 1,119 Palestinians and 51 Israelis have been killed in the West Bank since then, according to tallies and official figures cited by AFP [scmp.com#1].

title: Indonesia confirms 24 dead as rescuers search candy factory ruins
summary:
Indonesian authorities on Monday confirmed 24 deaths and said about 30 workers remained missing after a weekend fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, west of Jakarta [aljazeera.com#1][thehindu.com#1][theguardian.com#1]. Rescuers continued searching the burned site, where unstable structures and lingering hot spots endangered crews; 29 people were confirmed safe, including five who were hospitalized [aljazeera.com#1][thehindu.com#1].

The factory’s chief executive, Steven Erwin Wijaya, said about 300 people were at the complex for Saturday’s shift [thehindu.com#1][aljazeera.com#1]. Presidential labor adviser Said Iqbal said investigators were assessing whether safety protocols had been followed. He said preliminary information pointed to a possible air-conditioner short circuit, but authorities have not established the cause [thehindu.com#1][aljazeera.com#1].

The fire left many remains too badly damaged for visual identification, so police are collecting DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings. Identification could take two to three weeks [theguardian.com#1][aljazeera.com#1]. Search operations and the safety inquiry are continuing [thehindu.com#1][aljazeera.com#1].
quote: We are conducting sweeps in the areas that have already been brought under control
quote_author: Tubagus Mahfud, operations chief of the Serang fire department
talking_points: Rescue operation: More than 500 personnel, including soldiers, police, Red Cross workers and volunteers, searched an area of about 2,000 square metres [japantoday.com#1].
Affected area: Officials estimated 63 people were in the hardest-hit section, mostly on the second floor, where the fire reportedly began near a cooling unit [japantoday.com#1].
Company profile: The factory’s parent company employs about 5,000 people, and its Milkita candy products are exported to more than 40 countries [thehindu.com#1][japantoday.com#1].

perspectives.text: Said Iqbal, Indonesian presidential adviser on labor issues: Iqbal said he would summon the factory’s chief executive [thehindu.com#1].

Steven Erwin Wijaya, factory chief executive: Wijaya said the factory regularly held emergency and evacuation drills with local firefighters. He said evacuation routes and fire-protection systems met applicable standards and were working [theguardian.com#1].

Tubagus Mahfud, Serang fire department operations chief: Mahfud said collapsed sections and poor lighting forced firefighters to proceed cautiously. Production materials could reignite, requiring cooling operations before crews could enter all areas, he said [theguardian.com#1].

title: Federal government gives Toronto Santa Claus Parade up to $250,000
summary:
Canada’s federal government announced up to $250,000 for Toronto’s Original Santa Claus Parade on Nov. 22, the day the event’s 122nd edition drew crowds downtown. The grant is intended to improve the spectator experience, develop new ways to engage audiences and help keep the parade running. The government says the event attracts visitors and benefits local businesses [canada.ca#1][cbc.ca#1].

The free parade featured 23 floats and more than 1,500 marchers, with the Toronto Police Service’s mounted unit leading the procession from Christie Pits toward St. Lawrence Market [cbc.ca#1][torontotoday.ca#1][canada.ca#1]. Organizers described the federal contribution as support for future parades. The event attracts about 750,000 spectators annually and also reaches viewers through television and digital broadcasts [canada.ca#1].
quote: For generations, the Santa Claus Parade has brought holiday magic to Toronto’s streets. It brings families together, draws visitors downtown and supports local businesses along the route. Our government wants to help keep that tradition going strong. This investment will help make the parade experience even better and ensure it continues to bring joy to families and deliver benefits for local businesses for years to come.
quote_author: Evan Solomon, Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation and minister responsible for FedDev Ontario
talking_points: Route logistics: Construction near College Street prompted changes to the roughly seven-kilometre route, and police expected downtown road closures to end by 6 p.m. [torontosun.com#1][cp24.com#1]
Pre-parade event: A 5-kilometre Holly Jolly Fun Run was scheduled for 11:45 a.m., ahead of the parade’s 12:30 p.m. start [cp24.com#1].
Crowd conditions: Milder temperatures brought large crowds, with spectators lingering downtown after the procession passed [thestar.com#1].

title: Ontario Liberal leader Bains to meet caucus Monday without legislative seat
summary:
Ontario Liberal Leader Navdeep Bains is due to appear with his 14-member caucus at Queen’s Park on Monday, but he cannot challenge Premier Doug Ford in the legislature because he has no seat. Bains won the leadership of the third-place party on Saturday, narrowly defeating Toronto-area member of provincial parliament Lee Fairclough. He says he will seek elected office but has not identified a riding or timetable [theglobeandmail.com#1][cbc.ca#1].

Bains said he would first consult party executives and caucus members. He ruled out asking a sitting Liberal member to resign to make way for a by-election. He inherits a party that has struggled to regain ground since losing power in 2018 and says it must build a team and platform before the next election, which could be held as late as 2030 [theglobeandmail.com#1][cbc.ca#1][bramptonist.com#1].
quote: I will run after I engage with the party. I want to make sure I speak to the executive, speak to caucus as well.
talking_points: Close contest: About 37% of 56,000 eligible party voters cast ballots, up from 23% in the 2023 leadership election [nationalobserver.com#1].

Peel challenge: Progressive Conservatives won all five Brampton ridings in both the 2022 and 2025 provincial elections, although the Liberal share of the Brampton vote rose from 25.8% to 31.8% [bramptonist.com#1].
Campaign finances: Ontario Liberal president Kathryn McGarry said the party had paid off its 2025 campaign debt, allowing donor contributions to be directed toward the next campaign [cbc.ca#1].
Public profile: A Liaison Strategies survey of 1,600 Ontario voters during the leadership race found all four candidates were largely unknown to voters [nationalobserver.com#1].

perspectives.text: Ontario Premier Doug Ford: Ford congratulated Bains and urged parties to work together on tariffs, worker protection and affordability, saying families expect them to put the province ahead of party interests [theglobeandmail.com#1].
Ontario NDP Leader Marit Stiles: Stiles pointed to grocery prices, health-care wait times and high cellphone and internet bills as issues for which Ontarians want solutions [theglobeandmail.com#1].
Liberal strategist Theresa Lubowitz: Lubowitz argued that securing a legislative seat matters less than rebuilding the party through local outreach and grassroots work, riding by riding [cbc.ca#1].
Liberal strategist Charles Bird: Bird warned that the Progressive Conservatives could spend millions on negative advertising aimed at damaging the new leader’s reputation [cbc.ca#1].

title: Carney and party leaders trade jokes at Ottawa press dinner
summary:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shared the stage with comedians impersonating him and U.S. President Donald Trump at the annual Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner in Ottawa on Saturday. Journalists, politicians and lobbyists attended the traditional night of political satire. Carney joked about Trump’s Oval Office makeover and Canadian politics [cbc.ca#1][wral.com#1][sootoday.com#1].

Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre, Bloc Québécois Leader Yves-François Blanchet, New Democratic Party Leader Avi Lewis and Green Party Leader Mike Morrice also spoke. Carney left after his remarks, then watched Poilievre’s speech from the back of the room before departing; Poilievre stayed for the full dinner [cbc.ca#1][lapresse.ca#1].
quote: I am pressing the emergency comedy button.
talking_points: Telecom joke: Carney used a joke about oligopolies to refer to his remarks the previous week about Quebecor’s proposal to acquire telecom company Telus [cbc.ca#1][ledevoir.com#1].
Media funding: Poilievre ended his remarks by pretending to distribute money to journalists, mocking Liberal government funding for journalism [cbc.ca#1][sootoday.com#1].

Green leader: Newly elected Green Party Leader Mike Morrice joked about his own lack of a seat in Parliament and Poilievre’s loss of his Carleton riding in the 2025 federal election [cbc.ca#1][lapresse.ca#1].

Governor General: Governor General Louise Arbour joked that Carney was often away from Ottawa and made pointed remarks about homelessness, the residence at 24 Sussex and environmental work in Alberta [cbc.ca#1][ledevoir.com#1].

perspectives.text: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre: Poilievre portrayed Carney as controlling, citing reports that Carney yells at and micromanages staff and treats journalists poorly. He then joked that Carney was stealing his ideas [cbc.ca#1].
Bloc Québécois Leader Yves-François Blanchet: Blanchet broke from the roast format to say independent journalism is essential to democracy [cbc.ca#1][lapresse.ca#1].
New Democratic Party Leader Avi Lewis: Lewis joked about Carney’s early departure, saying he stayed for the full evening despite not having a seat in the House of Commons [cbc.ca#1].

title: U.S. trade chief says Canada deal is close, flags China ties
summary:
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Sunday that Canada and the United States are fairly close to a trade agreement, but warned that Canada’s expanding trade ties with China are a concern for Washington. Greer said negotiators were holding constructive talks on autos, steel and aluminum, but Canada’s chief trade negotiator, Janice Charette, told a federal advisory committee that several unresolved issues still block a deal [sootoday.com#1][globalnews.ca#1].

Talks collapsed in August after Ottawa rejected last-minute U.S. terms, including restrictions on future Canadian trade deals with other countries. Negotiations resumed this month, and officials in Prime Minister Mark Carney’s office said Carney and President Donald Trump agreed during a meeting in Shenzhen last week to keep working toward an agreement [globalnews.ca#1].
quote: We want to make sure that we’re protecting the North American economy while also landing on a deal that’s good for the United States and good for Canada
talking_points: Auto tariffs: The 25% U.S. tariff on Canadian automobiles is the largest outstanding issue, according to people briefed on the federal government’s discussions [globalnews.ca#1].
Chinese vehicles: Greer cited Canada’s plan to admit 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles annually at a lower tariff rate as a specific source of U.S. concern [globalnews.ca#1].

Trade balance: Greer said most goods traded between Canada and the United States still move duty-free and described the overall trade relationship as more positive than many people realize [sootoday.com#1].

perspectives.text: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s office: The office said a deal should create good jobs, improve affordability and fully respect Canada’s languages, culture and sovereignty [globalnews.ca#1].

title: ESA reports software-related thruster glitch during BepiColombo's Mercury arrival
summary:
The European Space Agency (ESA) said a software issue shortened one of BepiColombo’s thruster burns during its Mercury orbit insertion. The joint European-Japanese spacecraft entered orbit successfully on Nov. 21 and remains safe. Mission teams at the European Space Operations Centre are investigating the cause, and ESA said it would provide an update on Monday, Nov. 23 [thehindu.com#1][straitstimes.com#1][space.com#1].

BepiColombo carries two orbiters that have traveled together for eight years: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio. They are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with routine science operations planned to begin in April 2027 [thehindu.com#1][euronews.com#1][space.com#1].

The mission will investigate Mercury’s interior, magnetic field and surface, including the origins of its polar ice and unusual surface hollows. ESA said teams were investigating the issue and would provide further information on Monday [thehindu.com#1][space.com#1].
quote: I think it's a little bit of an under-loved planet in the inner Solar System, but I think that's one of the reasons why it is so compelling
quote_author: Professor Emma Bunce, University of Leicester principal investigator on the mission
talking_points: Different orbits: After separation, ESA’s orbiter is scheduled to pass as close as 480 kilometers from Mercury, while Japan’s Mio will follow an elliptical path reaching about 11,000 kilometers away [dir.bg#1].

Instrument payload: The European orbiter carries spectrometers, a surface altimeter and gravity-measuring instruments; its radio-science experiment will help determine the size of Mercury’s core [zmescience.com#1].

Swiss contribution: Neuchâtel company Micro-Cameras & Space Exploration built cameras to monitor spacecraft components and record flybys; University of Bern teams led development of the BELA laser altimeter and STROFIO mass spectrometer [lematin.ch#1].
Thermal challenge: Mercury’s surface can exceed 400°C, so mission engineers must keep the spacecraft and instruments cool while they operate in intense solar radiation [phys.org#1][japantoday.com#1].
Surface terrain: Mercury has expanses of smooth terrain as well as cliffs reaching about 1.6 kilometers high [thehindu.com#1].

perspectives.text: Professor Emma Bunce, a University of Leicester principal investigator on the mission, said its scientific goals range from understanding how Mercury formed and evolved to studying its interaction with the Sun and extreme space weather [bbc.co.uk#1].

Geraint Jones, BepiColombo’s lead project scientist, highlighted the mission’s ability to compare simultaneous measurements from two spacecraft at Mercury, describing the data as unprecedented [phys.org#1].

title: Deep-sea robot finds deepest volcanic deposits near Challenger Deep
summary:
The remotely operated vehicle Jason/Medea has found what researchers describe as the deepest documented underwater pyroclastic deposits, on the Mariana Trench wall about 6,000 meters below sea level [phys.org#1][livescience.com#1][sciencenews.org#1]. The rocks provide evidence of volcanic flows in the trench’s western forearc, where geologists expected little volcanic activity because the mantle is generally not hot enough to melt [phys.org#1][scimex.org#1]. The findings were published Nov. 23 in Frontiers in Earth Science [livescience.com#1][sciencenews.org#1].

The team’s observations support the idea that the Pacific Plate bends steeply as it sinks beneath the Mariana plate. That could help explain Challenger Deep’s depth and bring magma-generating processes closer to the trench [sciencenews.org#1][scimex.org#1]. But researchers have not identified the eruption sites or established how eruptions could produce these deposits under immense water pressure. They say further sampling and radiometric dating are needed. Jason/Medea cannot reach the seafloor below 6,500 meters, while Challenger Deep extends to about 11,000 meters [phys.org#1][scimex.org#1].
quote: Imagining this happening is … pretty mind-boggling.
quote_author: William Chadwick, geologist at Oregon State University
talking_points: Survey footprint: Jason/Medea made seven dives across roughly 300 kilometers of the forearc; researchers also examined the Shinaki Seep Field and retrieved fluid-sampling devices left by Japanese scientists in 2016 [phys.org#1][popsci.com#1].

Unlocated source: The pyroclastic flows appear to have traveled only a short distance because they retained enough heat to fuse into hard rock. They would have lost that heat on a longer journey [phys.org#1][scimex.org#1].

perspectives.text: Sune Nielsen, a geochemist at the University of Lorraine, described the finding as perplexing and said there was no clear explanation [livescience.com#1].
William Chadwick, a geologist at Oregon State University, said Challenger Deep may be uniquely suited to explosive volcanism in the super-deep ocean [sciencenews.org#1].

technical_details: Supercritical fluid hypothesis: Researchers propose that water released from magma could enter a supercritical state under extreme pressure, potentially producing dense, fragmented deposits without the gas expansion typical of surface eruptions. This mechanism has not been confirmed [livescience.com#1][sciencenews.org#1].

Forearc extension: The study distinguishes mechanical plate stretching, inferred from older eastern rocks, from the addition of magma, suggested by younger western volcanic rocks. Additional sampling and radiometric dating are needed to establish the difference [phys.org#1][scimex.org#1].
scientific_significance: Distinctive trench segment: Unlike the better-known volcanic-arc pattern, the Challenger Deep segment has no organized volcanic arc; an ocean ridge lies there instead [livescience.com#1].
Potential regional effects: As the forearc stretches, the associated subduction zone may widen, which researchers say could affect plate motions in the western Pacific [phys.org#1][scimex.org#1].
historical_background: The Mariana Trench formed about 52 million years ago as the Pacific Plate began sliding beneath the Philippine Sea Plate [phys.org#1][scimex.org#1].

title: Army schedules 68-barrel Iowa blast despite court-ordered pause
summary:
The U.S. Army plans to detonate 68 barrels of degraded lead azide on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, despite a federal appeals court order pausing the explosives disposal permit. The Army says it will rely on a separate emergency exception to proceed, arguing that the material could explode without warning as temperatures fall [straitstimes.com#1][cbsnews.com#1].

The Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice challenged the plan over the risk that a blast could spread lead-bearing dust. The Justice Department says a controlled detonation is safer than an uncontrolled explosion. The groups say invoking emergency powers would bypass the court’s review and have asked to submit additional evidence challenging the Army’s risk assessment [aljazeera.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1][cbsnews.com#1].

The Army moved the operation from Monday to Wednesday, saying the later date allows for favorable weather and time to put mitigation measures in place [kaaltv.com#1][straitstimes.com#1]. The groups’ legal challenge remains active, while the Army says it intends to proceed under the emergency exception [cbsnews.com#1][koat.com#1].
quote: Anyone can claim an emergency at any point and do whatever they want. I don’t think people can or should accept that.
talking_points: Alternative disposal: The Army hired a contractor to turn the explosives into harmless waste but later abandoned that approach in favor of detonating them in place [nytimes.com#3].

Range estimates: Army projections have varied. Iowa officials’ reporting cited a recent model showing lead dust settling across an area about 25 miles long and 5 miles wide, while earlier plume estimates extended as far as 100 miles, depending on weather [kaaltv.com#1][aljazeera.com#1].
Blast-control concerns: Environmental engineer Ranajit Sahu questioned whether the proposed controls would adequately protect public health [koat.com#1].

Farm concerns: Iowa agriculture officials advised nearby cattle farmers to move livestock, feed and equipment indoors or elsewhere, but farmers told the Iowa Environmental Council that keeping cattle indoors was not viable [straitstimes.com#1].
Local response: Mediapolis announced a school cancellation and library closure, and its school district said it would buy lead test kits to sample school grounds and buildings [futurism.com#1].

perspectives.text: U.S. Army: The Army says the doors to the explosives’ storage bunker were removed in preparation for the planned blast and cannot be reinstalled, leaving the material more exposed to temperature changes [wgnradio.com#1].

Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice: The groups say the Army’s storage and inspection practices allowed the lead azide to deteriorate, describing the emergency as one of the Army’s own making [koat.com#1].

Mark J. Thomas, former Environmental Protection Agency air-monitoring official: Thomas disputed the Army’s claim that cooling would make delay unsafe, saying the semi-underground structure would shield the drums from the full temperature change [koat.com#1].

Iowa Senator-elect Josh Turek: Turek called for a full investigation into why the stockpile was allowed to degrade, whether other dangerous materials are stored at the plant and how future failures can be prevented [cbsnews.com#1].

technical_details: Recrystallization: As liquid in the drums evaporated, needle-shaped lead azide crystals formed. The Army says the crystals are sensitive to friction and impact, making the barrels unsafe to open or move [aljazeera.com#1][wgnradio.com#1].
Blast controls: The Army’s plan uses earth-covered concrete magazines and sand barriers, with soil saturated and water sprayed before and during detonation to limit dust dispersal [shawlocal.com#1].
scientific_significance: Lead exposure: Lead can damage the brain and nervous system, particularly in children. The environmental groups are concerned that deposited particles could reach homes, farmland and waterways [straitstimes.com#1][kaaltv.com#1].

Exposure measurement: University of Iowa professor David Cwiertny said field sampling after the blast would be needed to determine where lead settles, since farm fields and topsoil cannot simply be wiped clean like household surfaces [aljazeera.com#1].

Uncertainty in plume models: The Army’s maps depend on real-time wind conditions, and reported projections differ in the area they predict will be affected. Air and surface sampling after the blast would measure actual exposure [aljazeera.com#1][kaaltv.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: Will Illinois also monitor for effects from the plume?
suggested_qna.answer: The Illinois Environmental Protection Agency said it would watch data from its northern Illinois air-monitoring network for signs of impacts on Illinois communities [shawlocal.com#1].

user_action_items: Follow local shelter and evacuation instructions if you are in the affected area: The Army advises people who cannot leave to remain indoors, close windows and doors, and turn off heating or cooling systems that bring in outside air during the exposure period [shawlocal.com#1].

Protect outdoor items and children’s play surfaces after officials end the exposure period: The Army advises wet-cleaning surfaces children may touch. Residents should follow local and Army guidance on when cleanup can begin [shawlocal.com#1].
humanitarian_impact: The blast could produce loud noise and ground vibrations, with officials warning that windows could break; residents near Middletown City Park and Butterfly Park were told to leave for six hours to avoid vibration risks [kaaltv.com#1][aljazeera.com#1].

title: November Beaver Moon begins series of close full moons through February
summary:
November’s full Beaver Moon peaks at 9:53 a.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, Nov. 24, when it will be below the horizon in North America. Observers there can look for it rising around sunset. The moon will be about 224,170 miles from Earth, close enough to qualify as a supermoon under some definitions, and should appear only slightly larger and brighter than an average full moon [livescience.com#1][usatoday.com#1][forbes.com#1].

The next full moon falls on Dec. 24 and is expected to be the closest in the sequence, at about 221,667 miles. Further full moons are due Jan. 22 and Feb. 20. Sources describe the sequence as either three or four consecutive supermoons [livescience.com#1][usatoday.com#1]. Near moonrise, the moon may look especially large because of the horizon-related “moon illusion,” not because it is closer at that moment [forbes.com#1][usatoday.com#1].
talking_points: Pleiades pairing: On Nov. 24, the moon will pass about 0.9 degrees from the Pleiades star cluster, though its brightness may obscure the cluster’s fainter stars [forbes.com#1].
Best viewing: The moon will appear full to the naked eye on Monday and Wednesday as well as Tuesday [livescience.com#1][nova.bg#1].

Coastal tides: People’s Daily Digital reported coastal preparations with sandbags, berms and pumps in Laguna Beach and other shoreline areas ahead of possible high-tide flooding [peopledaily.digital#1].
Other planets: On the night of Nov. 24-25, Mars and Jupiter are expected to be visible in the eastern sky, Saturn in the southwest, and Venus before dawn [mdr.de#1].
